newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan Wheat invests in Gdansk port.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan Wheat invests in Gdansk port.

text.p: Canada's largest grain handler said on Tuesday it acquired an US$8.0 million interest in a EuroPort Inc project to build and run a grain terminal at Poland's port of Gdansk, a statement said.
"The venture...positions the Pool in Eastern Europe to significantly enhance the co-operative's opportunities for expansion," Saskatchewan Wheat Pool president Leroy Larsen said in the statement.
SWP will invest US$8.0 million and 10 percent of the joint venture with an option to buy five percent more. It will provide construction expertise and then manage the terminal.
EuroPort Inc holds a long-term lease on 56 hectares (140 acres) of waterfront property and three berths at Gdansk's north port deep water pier, the statement said.

Gdansk is the deepest ice-free port in the Baltic Sea and can serve 60 million people within a 500 km (310 mile) radius, and could become the centre of grain import and export for Poland, Hungary, the Czech and Slovak Republics and the Commonwealth of Independent States, the statement said.
EuroPort Inc has exclusive rights to develop facilities to handle bulk grain, fertilizer, malt production, milling and other value-added grain and oilseed processing, SWP said.
SWP is Canada's largest grain handler with revenues of C$4.1 billioin in fiscal 1996 (Aug/July) and Canada's 54th largest company overall.
